metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Officially out for Week 12
metadata.description: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
metadata.analysis: DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Will miss time with hamstring injury
metadata.description: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that McGowan will miss some time after injuring his hamstring in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan (hamstring) to miss some time
metadata.description: Colts RB Seth McGowan is expected to miss "some time" with a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: McGowan suffered the injury in last Thursday's loss against the Texans. It is unclear if he is an IR candidate.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Will Miss Time With Hamstring Injury
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen said on Monday that rookie running back Seth McGowan (hamstring) "will miss some time" due to a hamstring injury that he suffered in Thursday night's loss to the division-rival Houston Texans, according to James Boyd of The Athletic. There is no exact timetable for McGowan's return, and the Colts probably will not rush him back in a lost season. The next question is whether the Colts will place McGowan on Injured Reserve, which would require him to sit out for at least four games. In the meantime, DJ Giddens will have short-term handcuff appeal in fantasy football leagues as the primary backup to starter Jonathan Taylor. The injury comes at a terrible time for the 25-year-old, who had a career game in the Week 10 win over the Miami Dolphins, when he had 12 rushing attempts for 77 yards and a rushing touchdown for the second straight week. McGowan had only three carries for seven yards and caught his only target for a one-yard gain in last Thursday's loss to Houston, though, and now he is out for the foreseeable future. Indy's backfield has been their lone bright spot on offense in 2026, and McGowan, a seventh-rounder, has been a big reason why, with an average of 5.0 yards per carry for 292 yards and two touchdowns as the complement to JT.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Remains a Must-Add Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts rookie running back Seth McGowan (hamstring) remains a must-add off the waiver wire after his continued usage in the offense over the past five weeks, averaging nine opportunities a game. It's clear the Colts will not be competitive in 2026 (3-8 record), and they cut Daniel Jones after his Week 11 performance and shipped out star players at the trade deadline. Jonathan Taylor remains the last man standing, raising a huge question mark about how the Colts should and will utilize him for the rest of the season, considering it's possible he gets traded; therefore, it's likely in their best interest to limit Taylor's workload, leaving McGowan open for opportunities and as a strong handcuff. While McGowan hasn't gotten much opportunity, he has been extremely efficient on the touches he has earned, ranking sixth in yards per carry, third in EPA per attempt, and second in rush success rate. Due to his continued efficiency, he should remain rostered heading into Week 12.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan gets four touches, leaves with injury Thursday night
metadata.description: Seth McGowan gained seven yards on three carries and just one yard on one catch before exiting Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans with a hamstring injury.
metadata.analysis: McGowan had been a bright spot for the struggling Colts in recent weeks, as the rookie back has looked like a capable ball carrier behind veteran Jonathan Taylor. Unfortunately, he sustained a hamstring injury after just a few touches Thursday night and did not return to the contest. McGowan has averaged an impressive 5.0 yards on his 58 total carries with two touchdowns so far this season. He's got plenty of fantasy value sharing the backfield with Taylor as long as the injury doesn't force him to miss time.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Won't return to Thursday Night Football
metadata.description: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Questionable to return to TNF
metadata.description: McGowan is dealing with a hamstring injury and is questionable to return to Thursday's Week 11 game against Houston.
metadata.analysis: McGowan appeared to get injured while returning a kickoff just before halftime. The rookie running back had three carries for seven yards and one catch for one yard before getting hurt. Should McGowan not be able to return to action Thursday, Jonathan Taylor would likely get an even bigger share of carries for the Colts, and DJ Giddens should get more opportunities as well.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Ruled Out for Remainder of Thursday's Game
metadata.description: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out running back Seth McGowan (hamstring) for the rest of the Thursday night game against the division-rival Houston Texans after he injured his hamstring towards the end of the first half on a kickoff, according to Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Sports. It ends a disappointing night for the 25-year-old rookie after his career-best performance in the Week 10 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, when he had 12 carries for 77 yards and his second touchdown in as many weeks. Before leaving on Thursday in Houston, McGowan had only three carries for seven yards and one catch for a gain of one yard. Jonathan Taylor will now see more backfield touches for the Colts for the rest of the game, with DJ Giddens stepping up in a complementary role. The good news for McGowan is that he will have more time to recover before Indy's next game in Week 12 at home against the New York Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29. McGowan has become much more involved for the Colts alongside Taylor in recent weeks, making him a priority handcuff addition in fantasy football leagues now that Taylor is still in Indy following the trade deadline.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Worth Considering in All Leagues
metadata.description: Indianapolis running back Seth McGowan has scored touchdowns in back-to-back games and has carved out a big enough offensive role to consider possibly starting him in all fantasy football leagues for Week 11. His matchup against the Texans on Thursday night is pretty average. The teams met back in Week 3, when McGowan wasn't nearly as big an offensive threat for Indianapolis. Along with a score in two straight games, McGowan has 122 rushing yards over 18 attempts. He has five or more rushing attempts in four straight games now, and with more production of late, he's a rising fantasy asset. McGowan is RB34 in our RotoBaller Week 11 projections, putting him outside most standard leagues, but also close enough to be a flex-level option for some fantasy squads. He's worth starting in most deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan punches in score in win over Dolphins
metadata.description: Seth McGowan ran for 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McGowan wasn't involved in the passing game, but when you can run for 6.4 yards a pop and find the end zone, that makes up for a lot. He is becoming more involved in the offense in recent weeks and could be finding his way into flex territory. Granted, touchdowns have greatly helped his fantasy production, without them he would be much less appealing.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Is a Week 11 Bench Stash
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan carried the ball on 12 of his 17 offensive snaps against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. He finished with 77 yards and a touchdown after rushing for 45 yards and a score on six carries against the Dallas Cowboys. His snap share slipped from 31% to 29% across those games. Before Sunday, he'd reached double-digit carries just once, with 11 against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Both touchdowns came from inside the five-yard line, giving McGowan some flex appeal in 14-team half-PPR leagues on Thursday at Houston. McGowan has five catches for nine yards all season, and Jonathan Taylor drew all four backfield targets against Miami. Taylor also led Indianapolis with 16 carries and played 40 offensive snaps. Rostered in 18% of Yahoo leagues, McGowan is worth a bench spot in 12-team half-PPR leagues, especially for Taylor managers. McGowan handled every other running back touch against Miami, and DJ Giddens played just two offensive snaps. That split puts McGowan first in line for more carries if Taylor misses time.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Retains expanded role Sunday
metadata.description: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Scores Again on Career-High 12 Carries
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan picked up the final first down of Sunday's 24-22 win over the Miami Dolphins with consecutive runs of eight and four yards, allowing Indianapolis to kneel out the clock. He finished with a career-high 12 carries for 77 yards and a touchdown. McGowan gained eight yards on the final play of the first quarter and scored from four yards out on the next snap. He later broke a 23-yard run to Miami's one-yard line. Jonathan Taylor took the next handoff and lost a yard. McGowan had eight carries by halftime to Taylor's nine. Taylor finished with 83 yards on 16 carries and caught two of four targets for 20 yards. McGowan went without a target. McGowan also scored from two yards out against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 9, taking over on third down after Taylor's six-yard run. He had four carries for 14 yards against the Houston Texans in Week 3. His recent chances near the goal line give him flex appeal in deeper leagues for Thursday's rematch at Houston.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan a Deep-League Option in Week 10 in Reserve Role
metadata.description: Indianapolis running back Seth McGowan is just a deep-league fantasy option due to Jonathan Taylor remaining with the team after the trade deadline. McGowan has carved out a decent offensive role though, carrying the ball 43 times for 208 yards and a touchdown so far, while also hauling in five of his six targets for nine yards. He has played 22.3% of the team's offensive snaps so far. Miami is a pretty favorable matchup for running backs, so McGowan has a little fantasy appeal, but just in deeper leagues. He's RB46 in our RotoBaller Week 10 projections, showing he's only startable in deeper setups. McGowan would only become a standard league option if Taylor were injured, so that's something to keep in mind, especially with the Colts' season fading away.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan's Fantasy Value Hinges on Potential Trade
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts rookie running back Seth McGowan had six carries for 45 yards and a touchdown, along with one reception for minus-three yards in the 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. As McGowan continues to carve out a role behind starting Jonathan Taylor, the rookie scored his first career touchdown from two yards out. Taylor has been involved in trade talks, and he said postgame, "I just hope that they appreciate and know that I appreciate them and it was a pleasure to put on display not only my hard work but the team's hard work each and every single week, each and every single year. Just know it was a pleasure." If Taylor is dealt prior to Tuesday's deadline, McGowan should factor in as a low-end RB2, assuming no other backs are traded to Indianapolis. McGowan's value hinges on a Taylor trade, as he doesn't offer enough value as a handcuff in this struggling offensive attack.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Gets into end zone in loss
metadata.description: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan finds the end zone in Week 9
metadata.description: Seth McGowan carried the ball six times for 45 yards and a touchdown while losing three yards on his lone reception in a 27-23 loss to the Cowboys in Week 9.
metadata.analysis: McGowan punched in a two-yard touchdown in the first quarter to give the Colts their first points of the game. The rookie running back could be the team's starting running back in Week 10 against the Dolphins if the Colts wind up trading Jonathan Taylor by Tuesday's trade deadline. McGowan would be a locked-in RB2 in fantasy for Week 10 if that were to happen.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan is Too Risky To Start
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan remains a top stash target ahead of the trade deadline. It sounds likely that the Colts will keep Jonathan Taylor, but fantasy managers should stash McGowan just in case. Last week, McGowan carried the ball five times for 29 yards during the blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. With Taylor possibly leaving, McGowan could see an expanded role during the Week 9 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. It's a favorable matchup with the Cowboys having the worst run defense in the league. Despite it being a great matchup, McGowan is too risky to start in fantasy formats with Taylor still on the team. The 25-year-old is worth stashing, but he isn't an ideal streaming option for Week 9.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Breaks one long run Week 8
metadata.description: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that Giddens didn't enter until the fourth quarter and racked up all of his yardage in garbage time.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan a Priority Stash Ahead of Trade Deadline
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan should be stashed in most 12+ team fantasy football leagues ahead of the NFL's trade deadline on Nov. 10. There have been plenty of trade rumors circulating around Jonathan Taylor, and if he ends up being dealt, McGowan would take over as Indianapolis' undisputed No. 1 running back. It would take a lot for the Colts to trade Taylor, but it does seem like the rumors have been gaining steam over the last couple of days. Indianapolis has done a good job getting McGowan more involved lately, as he played 34% of the snaps in Week 7 and has totaled 17 touches across his last two games. The 25-year-old rookie from Kentucky would be the Colts' top fantasy running back if Taylor gets dealt, but even then, he'd likely rank as a high-end RB3 with a moderately low floor. After all, Indianapolis looks pretty weak on offense, so there may not be a ton of high-value touches for McGowan, even if he does end up leading the backfield throughout the second half of the season.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan gets five carries in Sunday's loss
metadata.description: Seth McGowan gained 29 yards on five carries in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: McGowan's name, rightly so, has been increasingly popping up on the fantasy radar as trade rumors have built around Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor. Sunday's game got out of hand by halftime, so the Colts mostly went away from the running game. However, if Taylor is indeed traded away, McGowan could see plenty of work during the second half of the season. The rookie out of Kentucky has averaged 4.4 yards on 37 total carries so far.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Still Firmly the Colts' RB2 For Now
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts backup running back Seth McGowan hasn't seen more than a handful of touches in any of his games this season, and that's unlikely to change in Week 8. The Colts will take on the Jacksonville Jaguars, and Indianapolis RB1 Jonathan Taylor, who remains with the team for now despite trade rumors swirling, will be the clear workhorse running back as long as he is under contract with them. Taylor is one of the NFL's best running backs, and would be the clear starter on any team that was willing to trade for him or the Colts if they decide to keep him. McGowan saw 11 rushes and one target in Week 7, totaling a season-high 12 touches, but even that was uncharacteristically high for him. McGowan is a priority waiver pickup in all leagues before Week 8's Sunday slate of games, as many fantasy managers are flocking to pick him up with Taylor's potential exit looming. But he should be left on benches as long as Taylor is still with the Colts and expected to start.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Rushes 11 times in loss
metadata.description: McGowan turned 11 carries into 46 yards, caught his only target for two yards and added 140 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
metadata.analysis: McGowan played a season-high 31 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to set new highs in both carries and rushing yards. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded in the coming weeks, the rookie would stand to operate as the team's lead back following Taylor's departure. On the season, McGowan has rushed 34 times for 134 yards and reeled in four of five targets for 12 yards while compiling 566 kickoff-return yards over seven contests so far.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan a Priority Waiver-Wire Stash Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts rookie running back Seth McGowan has played a limited role in his team's offense so far in 2026, recording 146 yards from scrimmage on 36 touches across seven games. The 25-year-old had his usage scaled up in Week 7, logging 11 carries for 46 yards against the Minnesota Vikings. McGowan's growing role could be a sign of things to come. The Colts still have superstar running back Jonathan Taylor firmly ahead of McGowan on the depth chart, which will not change as long as Taylor remains healthy and on the roster. However, with the Colts currently sitting at 2-5 and riding a three-game losing streak, trade speculation around Taylor has begun to heat up. If Taylor were to get moved, McGowan could be in line to assume a workhorse role in the Indianapolis backfield. In leagues where he is available on the waiver wire, McGowan profiles as a priority stash candidate as the trade deadline approaches.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan sees 11 carries Sunday
metadata.description: Seth McGowan ran for 46 yards on 11 carries in the Colts 16-10 loss against the Vikings. He also caught his lone target for two yards receiving.
metadata.analysis: McGowan saw a season-high in carries, his first time reaching double-digit carries. He is an intriguing stash for fantasy managers with Jonathan Taylor continuing to have his name brought up in trade rumors.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan a Top Stash as Teammate's Trade Rumors Heat Up
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan is a priority waiver wire target, given that he has the potential to ascend into the No. 1 role over the next few weeks. Trade rumors are heating up surrounding Jonathan Taylor, with several teams expected to have interest if the Colts continue to lose games and trade away some of their top talent. McGowan is the direct backup to Taylor, and he would presumably handle the lead-back role if Taylor were to be traded. While we wouldn't expect McGowan to slot in as a mid-range RB1 in fantasy football, his talent and presumptive volume could at least get him on the RB2 radar, as we don't expect he'd have a ton of competition from DJ Giddens, who has yet to play an offensive snap this year. There's definitely a possibility that the Colts keep Taylor, and McGowan doesn't get onto the fantasy radar this year. However, there's also a possibility that McGowan becomes a weekly fantasy starter in this hypothetical Colts backfield without Taylor. As a result, he's a worthwhile stash in 12+ team redraft leagues and almost all dynasty formats.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Efficient on low volume Sunday
metadata.description: McGowan took four carries for 27 yards during Sunday's 26-20 loss versus the Titans.
metadata.analysis: McGowan played exactly 19 offensive snaps for the third straight week Sunday, and although he was slightly less involved than he has been of late in terms of touches, he managed a career-best 6.8 yards per carry in Week 6. He's merely a change-of-pace back as long as three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor is healthy, but he has the physical traits to become a workhorse should that not be the case at any point this season.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan a Top Handcuff to Look for on Waivers
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts rookie running back Seth McGowan has seen modest involvement in each of the past four games, showing enough to make him an attractive handcuff behind three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor. With the Colts in free fall at 2-4 and having recently fired longtime general manager Chris Ballard, there is also an outside chance the team could look to move Taylor ahead of the NFL's November 10th trade deadline. A seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, McGowan is the only other running back on Indianapolis' roster to receive a carry through six games, averaging more than four yards per attempt, and with multiple paths to an increased workload, he makes for an intriguing long-term stash in a week with few high-priority waiver targets.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan runs for 27 yards in loss
metadata.description: Seth McGowan ran four times for 27 yards in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McGowan is once again playing backup to Jonathan Taylor, which is unlikely to change. Keep him stashed on your bench if you have Taylor.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Among the Top Handcuffs to Stash
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan has emerged as one of the more appealing handcuff stashes in fantasy football, with a clear path to increased opportunities if Jonathan Taylor misses time. The 6-foot, 223-pound rookie has established himself as Indianapolis' primary backup, while DJ Giddens has yet to play an offensive snap this season. McGowan has recorded 17 carries for 61 yards and three receptions for 10 yards through five games, including five rushes for 16 yards and one catch for three yards in Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. He played 26.1% of the offensive snaps in that contest after reaching a season-high 29% in Week 4. Taylor continues to dominate the backfield, playing 82.2% of Indianapolis' offensive snaps through five games, leaving McGowan with little standalone fantasy value. However, the rookie's size, established position on the depth chart, and limited competition behind him make him an attractive insurance option. Taylor managers should strongly consider rostering McGowan, while those in deeper leagues can justify stashing him before an injury potentially sends his waiver value soaring.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan sees six touches in loss
metadata.description: Seth McGowan ran five times for 16 yards and caught his only target for three yards in the Colts' 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: McGowan was the clear No.2 back behind Jonathan Taylor yet again, but it didn't amount to much for fantasy. He's a clear-cut handcuff and not a bad one to have, but it's unlikely he will garner enough of a workload to really warrant starting him without a Taylor injury.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan A Waiver Target As Handcuff RB For Colts
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan appears to have fully wrested control of his team's RB2 job away from DJ Giddens, the other RB on the roster aside from starter Jonathan Taylor. Giddens dealt with a knee injury in Week 2, but was a healthy scratch for Week 3, as the coaching staff decided to make Taylor and McGowan the team's active running backs. There is essentially zero chance that McGowan will push the coaching staff to hand him more touches at the expense of Taylor, who's one of the best backs in the league. But the rookie would step into a large role if Taylor got injured, meaning he should be added by fantasy managers who want to handcuff Taylor and in deeper leagues where all RB2s are rostered. McGowan is a nice lottery ticket in an offense that was highly productive last season before quarterback Daniel Jones tore his Achilles tendon. He's been active and starting for the first four games, but likely still needs time to heal. McGowan could see 20 or more touches in games that Taylor misses. He carried the ball six times for 31 yards and caught one of his two targets for seven yards in a dominant win over the Washington Commanders in Week 4 while Giddens sat on the sideline, so it's obvious McGowan is the target to pickup off waivers.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Seven touches in Week 4 victory
metadata.description: McGowan turned six carries into 31 yards and caught one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
metadata.analysis: McGowan actually saw most of his offensive output in the second quarter with four carries for 18 yards and his seven-yard catch. Most of his on-field production figures to come on special teams as a returner, but the rookie seventh-rounder would be thrust into RB1 duties if Jonathan Taylor were to miss time. The Colts will hit the road for Week 5 against the Steelers this Sunday.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Remains Stash Option
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan saw the most action of the season during the Week 3 win over the Houston Texans. McGowan rushed the ball four times for 14 yards in the two-point victory. The 24-year-old has seen a minimal role in the backfield over the first three weeks of the season. His role is unlikely to grow much with Jonathan Taylor being the workhorse back in Indy right now. The rookie back is still one of the more interesting handcuff options around the league. McGowan could be one injury away from being the starter in an offense that loves to run the ball. He's worth stashing in deep leagues and dynasty formats on the chance that Taylor misses time.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan is Unlikely to See Consistent Role
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan has barely seen the field over the first two games of the regular season. Heading into Week 3, McGowan has registered two carries for zero yards and one reception for zero yards. The 24-year-old is unlikely to have standalone value while Jonathan Taylor is healthy. Taylor is the workhorse back, and McGowan only saw the field for six percent of the offensive snaps last week. He remains worth stashing because he could see a significant role if Taylor ever goes down with an injury. Fantasy managers shouldn't bother starting McGowan in any formats ahead of the Week 3 matchup against the Houston Texans.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Is a Pure Contingency Play
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan has barely touched the ball through two games, but his spot on the depth chart is what keeps him interesting. McGowan caught one pass for no gain in Week 1, then had two carries for no yards against Kansas City. Jonathan Taylor has handled 43 carries and seven receptions over that same stretch, so there is no standalone role to chase. McGowan is still listed directly behind Taylor, though, and DJ Giddens has been inactive for both games. The rookie has played just 11.1% of the offensive snaps, which makes this a pure contingency bet. RotoBaller includes McGowan among its high-upside handcuffs and ranks him 52nd overall on the Week 3 waiver board, with an add recommendation in 14-team leagues. He is not worth forcing onto a shallow roster, but deeper-league managers looking for a direct backup to one of the league's busiest backs can justify stashing him now.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Zero offensive yards in loss
metadata.description: McGowan rushed twice for zero yards and had two kick returns for 58 yards in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: McGowan saw just four offensive snaps in the contest, receiving the ball on two of them. The seventh-round rookie did not make a strong impression against the Chiefs' defensive line, but was able to prove useful on special teams with a 29-yard average on kick returns.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Remains a Worthy Deep-League Handcuff Running Back
metadata.description: A seventh-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan has begun his first NFL season in a reserve role behind superstar Colts back Jonathan Taylor. As long as Taylor remains healthy, McGowan is highly unlikely to see a fantasy-relevant workload. In the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens, the 23-year-old recorded zero carries and one catch for zero yards on one target. Still, McGowan cemented his status as the Colts' RB2, as he was the only back besides Taylor to see the field against Baltimore. Taylor has recorded over 700 touches since the start of the 2024 season, and he appears to be on his way to another massive workload in 2026. If he were to go down with an injury at any point, McGowan could immediately vault into fantasy relevance. In deeper leagues, McGowan could be worth targeting on the waiver wire for his handcuff appeal.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Scarcely used offensively in Week 1
metadata.description: McGowan caught his only target for no gain and notched 164 yards on five kick returns during Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: McGowan was only on the field for six of the team's 54 offensive snaps while operating as the top reserve option at running back behind Jonathan Taylor. McGowan definitely made his mark on special teams during the contest, but as long as Taylor is healthy, he will likely have a limited impact on offense.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan catches one pass in Week 1
metadata.description: Seth McGowan caught his only target for no gain in the Colts' 41-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: McGowan was one of many options in the Indianapolis offense that failed to make an impact in the Week 1 loss and can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a tough Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan's Long Road Leads to the Colts' RB2 Job
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan took a long route to his current spot behind Jonathan Taylor. Joel A. Erickson of the Indianapolis Star detailed the difficult road McGowan traveled after his career at Oklahoma ended following a 2021 arrest, with stops at Texas College, Butler Community College, New Mexico State and Kentucky before the Colts drafted him in the seventh round this spring. The football climb continued once he arrived. McGowan impressed Indianapolis with his physical running and receiving ability during camp, and he has now moved ahead of DJ Giddens on the current depth chart after opening the preseason behind him. That makes the rookie considerably more interesting for fantasy. Taylor still dominates this backfield, so there isn't much standalone value to chase right now. McGowan has nevertheless gone from a seventh-round flier to the Colts' No. 2 back, giving him real handcuff value if his role is ever forced to grow.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Requires Patience in Deeper Fantasy Leagues
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan is more of a bench swing than somebody fantasy managers should expect to use anytime soon. The seventh-round rookie made the 53-man roster after rushing for 725 yards and 12 touchdowns at Kentucky last season, and the Colts liked the physicality he showed throughout the preseason. There is still somebody in his way before Jonathan Taylor, though. Indianapolis currently lists DJ Giddens second on the depth chart and McGowan third, leaving the rookie without much of a standalone role heading into Week 1. The good news is that the Colts kept only three running backs on the active roster, so an injury could change things quickly. McGowan is rostered in just 1% of Yahoo leagues and sits in the 14-team range on the current waiver list. That's where he belongs for now. Deep benches can take the shot, but managers in standard leagues do not need to force it.

metadata.title: Colts Running Back Seth McGowan Turning Heads In Preseason
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts backup running back Seth McGowan is projected to win the handcuff job to lead back Jonathon Taylor according to The Athletic's James Boyd. In an August 29 article, Boyd wrote, "McGowan has clearly won the second-string job thanks to his physicality and reliable hands out of the backfield." The seventh-round pick out of Kentucky in the 2026 Draft, McGowan stands at 6-foot-1 and is 223 pounds offering big-time size out of the backfield but as Boyd points out he can catch the ball as well and thus be involved in the passing game. McGowan had two catches for five yards each in the three preseason games and rushed 17 times for 64 yards. With McGowan seeming to prove himself as the backup to Taylor look for him as a very late round pick or a potential early season waiver wire option.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan - Gets start in final preseason contest
metadata.description: McGowan carried the ball four times for 20 yards and caught his only target for five yards in Saturday's 25-16 preseason loss to the Lions.
metadata.analysis: The seventh-round rookie got the start once again, even with DJ Giddens back in the lineup after recovering from a hamstring injury, and McGowan put together the Colts' longest run of the afternoon on a 10-yard scamper in the first quarter to help set up a field goal. Giddens scored the team's only TD of the game in the second quarter, however, as they both make their final cases to be the No. 2 backfield option behind Jonathan Taylor. The two younger backs had similar athleticism-over-production profiles in college, so they could end up trading the job back and forth during the season based on health and performance.

metadata.title: Seth McGowan Likely Does Enough to Win the Backup Job
metadata.description: Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan rushed for 20 yards on five carries during Saturday's preseason contest against the Detroit Lions. He also had a five-yard reception in the loss. McGowan finished the preseason with 74 scrimmage yards across three games, and he might have done enough to win the backup job behind Jonathan Taylor. Entering the summer, the backup competition was between McGowan and DJ Giddens, a 2025 fifth-round pick who had 96 rushing yards last year. In addition to out-producing Giddens this preseason, McGowan is younger, although he has slightly lower draft capital as a seventh-round pick. It's important to note that both running backs are merely competing for a handcuff role here, as Jonathan Taylor is the undisputed every-down back in Indianapolis. Taylor was responsible for a whopping 86.6% of the Colts' running back carries last year, and he figures to achieve a similar mark in 2026. If McGowan is confirmed as Taylor's backup, he'll still be avoidable in shallower redraft leagues, and he'll be a mere stash in dynasty and deeper redraft formats.
